coastal.title: Firefighters dealing with abandoned, 'intentionally-set' fires on Sunshine Coast
coastal.description: "We are monitoring the situation very, very closely in regards to enacting a campfire prohibition," said fire Chief Dwight Davison.

kamloops.title: About 150 structures damaged, destroyed by Bald Range wildfire, as most of Summerland returns
kamloops.description: The Bald Range wildfire is still listed as out of control and has now grown to 21,391 hectares since it was discovered 11 days ago.

kamloops.title: Take a bough: Climbing takes relationship with B.C.’s trees to the next level
kamloops.description: Tom Zadorsky is part of a movement that aims to awaken a climbers' inner child and give a new perspective on British Columbia's forests.

kamloops.title: Summerland residents begin returning home as roughly 1,200 properties cleared for re-entry
kamloops.description: After more than a week, some Summerland residents are finally walking back through their front doors.

kamloops.title: What you need to know about B.C. wildfires on Aug. 18
kamloops.description: Thousands of Summerland residents were given the go-ahead to return home on Tuesday as the district lifted the majority of evacuation orders related to the Bald Range fire.

kamloops.title: Evacuation order lifted for majority of Summerland, with about 150 structures believed damaged
kamloops.description: Thousands of Summerland residents are allowed to make their way home Tuesday, more than a week after the Bald Range wildfire forced them to flee.

prince-george.title: Carney says last-minute U.S. tariff negotiations are 'delicate' and 'intense' as deadline looms
prince-george.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said last-minute negotiations with the U.S. to avoid a fresh batch of tariffs due to take effect this week are "delicate" and "intense," and he plans to speak to his American counterpart in the next 48 hours to broker a mutually agreeable deal.

all.title: B.C. wildfire latest: Thousands of people still out of their homes, but there is some good news
all.description: B.C. provincial health officer Dr. Bonnie Henry is set to hold a news conference Tuesday as much of the southern half of the province remains blanketed in wildfire smoke.
